title: The Stability Gap in Continual Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.26252v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Continual reinforcement learning (CRL) aims to enable agents to adapt to changing tasks while preserving previously acquired capabilities. Evaluation often relies on final aggregate metrics that can hide temporary performance degradation during adaptation. This work introduces a simple CRL benchmark that varies observation representations while preserving environment dynamics and rewards, supporting proof-of-concept demonstrations, inexpensive experimentation, and easily reproducible sanity checks. Using this benchmark, we demonstrate the stability gap in CRL: a substantial drop in prior-task performance after the introduction of new tasks, followed by partial or complete recovery. This pattern occurs despite the agent having complete access to past tasks.

translated_title: 持续强化学习中的稳定性差距
translated_abstract: 持续强化学习（CRL）旨在使智能体能够适应不断变化的任务，同时保留之前获得的能力。评估通常依赖于最终的聚合指标，而这些指标可能掩盖适应过程中的临时性能下降。本工作引入了一个简单的持续强化学习基准，该基准在保持环境动态和奖励不变的情况下改变观测表示，支持概念验证演示、低成本实验以及易于重现的健全性检查。利用这个基准，我们展示了持续强化学习中的稳定性差距：在引入新任务后，先前任务的性能出现大幅下降，随后部分或完全恢复。尽管智能体可以完全访问过去的任务，这种模式仍然会发生。
tldr: 本文提出了一个在保持环境动态和奖励不变的前提下仅改变观测表示的简单持续强化学习基准，并首次揭示了其中的“稳定性差距”现象——即使智能体可以完全访问过去任务，新任务的引入仍会导致旧任务性能大幅下降后再部分或完全恢复。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a simple continual RL benchmark that varies observation representations while preserving environment dynamics and rewards, and reveals the "stability gap" phenomenon: even with full access to past tasks, the introduction of new tasks causes a substantial drop in prior-task performance followed by partial or complete recovery.
